title: PipeRAG: Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Adaptive Pipeline Parallelism

problem.claim: Retrieval from large token databases can substantially increase RAG generation time, especially when retrieval is performed periodically to align retrieved content with the latest generation states.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a need to co-design RAG algorithms and underlying systems to reduce retrieval-related latency while maintaining or improving generation quality.

contributions.claim: PipeRAG combines pipeline parallelism, flexible retrieval intervals, and a performance model for balancing retrieval quality and latency according to generation states and hardware.
PipeRAG enables concurrent retrieval and generation processes through pipeline parallelism.
PipeRAG uses flexible retrieval intervals and a performance model to balance retrieval quality and latency.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce PipeRAG as a novel algorithm-system co-design approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The evaluation reports up to 2.6× speedup in end-to-end generation latency while improving generation quality.
The authors describe the results as demonstrating the effectiveness of co-designing algorithms with underlying systems for future RAG systems.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG improves LLM generation quality by incorporating external token databases.
Large-database retrieval can become a major part of generation time, particularly with periodic retrieval.
PipeRAG introduces an algorithm-system co-design using concurrent retrieval and generation, flexible retrieval intervals, and hardware-aware performance modeling.
The authors report up to 2.6× lower end-to-end generation latency together with improved generation quality.
The reported results support applying algorithm-system co-design to future RAG systems.

source_observation.claim: Concurrent retrieval and generation, combined with adaptive retrieval intervals, are presented as mechanisms for reducing RAG latency.

interpretation.claim: Latency-sensitive retrieval systems may benefit from coordinating algorithmic scheduling with system-level parallelism.

application.claim: When designing retrieval-generation pipelines, model retrieval intervals and hardware behavior jointly rather than optimizing retrieval quality in isolation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported tradeoff generalizes across datasets, hardware configurations, or workload patterns.

unknowns: Evaluation datasets, workloads, baselines, and hardware configurations are unspecified.
The generation-quality metric and the conditions for the reported 2.6× speedup are unspecified.
The performance model's inputs, optimization procedure, and overhead are unspecified.
